The DexTor OS image now comes from dextoros.com only, the launcher hands the Windows time zone
to DexTor OS, the local journals keep less, and the end-user license is updated to version 1.4.
This release follows v0.1.40; the versions in between were internal test builds.

DexTor OS is also in the Microsoft Store: <https://apps.microsoft.com/detail/9N23N99XWH3V>.
The Store delivers its own updates after Microsoft's review, so the version there can differ
from this release.

## Highlights

- **The image is downloaded from https://dextoros.com only.** Every build of the launcher
  fetches the DexTor OS image, its SHA-256 and its signature from `https://dextoros.com` and
  nowhere else. If the release index names any other address, the launcher requests nothing
  from it and says "The download address is not on dextoros.com". It no longer follows
  redirects for these downloads. The signature and hash checks are unchanged.
  QEMU is still downloaded from DexTor's mirror, with qemu.weilnetz.de as a fallback.
- **The Windows time zone is passed to DexTor OS.** When DexTor OS starts inside Windows, the
  launcher hands it the name of the Windows time zone as an IANA name, for example
  `Europe/Berlin`, next to the language. Only the name is passed: the virtual machine's clock
  stays in UTC, and applying the zone is up to DexTor OS. Nothing is passed when Windows' zone
  has no IANA name. Like the rest of the QEMU command line, the name is written to the VM
  session log in `%LOCALAPPDATA%\DexTor\Sessions`, which stays on your computer.
- **Less in the local journals.** The USB creation journal no longer records the Windows user
  name; earlier versions wrote it to the journal's first line, in a file that never left the
  computer. The step-by-step `.log` of each creation is now removed together with its journal:
  the last 20 are kept, older ones go once they are more than 30 days old.
- **EULA version 1.4.** `EULA.md`, attached to this release, replaces version 1.0 for this and
  later releases; v0.1.39 and v0.1.40 stay under the version they shipped with. It names the
  parties more precisely, states that it adds permissions for the release builds and does not
  restrict rights under the source code license or third-party licenses, describes the limits
  of running DexTor OS in a window on a Windows host, and has a "Disputes" section.

## Fixes and changes

- The installer no longer has an "I agree" checkbox. The line with the link to the license
  terms now says that clicking Install accepts them, in all 10 languages.
- The version number has left the footer. Rest the pointer on the DexTor OS logo to see it,
  for example "DexTor OS for Windows v0.1.45".
- The glow of the main button fades in and out over 180 ms instead of switching at once, and is
  drawn as one rounded shape without seams in the corners. The installer's button images are
  redrawn the same way.
- Wizard texts, in all 10 languages: "From a compatible PC" instead of "From any PC"; "Beta
  version written and verified" on the Ready screen; the Guest and Secure mode notice as two
  plain sentences; status values start with a capital letter ("Turned on", "Verified",
  "Matches"); free disk space is shown as the size alone.
- `THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md` has a Microsoft Store column and says plainly that hosting the QEMU
  mirror is distribution by DexTor, with the corresponding source published next to it.
- The README screenshots are retaken from this version, and the README has a "Get it" section
  with the Microsoft Store and the portable file. The security policy, the bug report form and
  the packaging notes say where the version is shown now, that data is kept in the local
  application data folder, and that Windows asks for administrator approval both to write the
  USB drive and to turn on the Windows Hypervisor Platform.

## Download

`DexTorOS-Portable-0.1.45-win-x64.exe` - one portable file, no installation and no separate .NET
needed. Requires Windows 11 x64. It was built from exactly the source code of this release
with `build-portable.bat 0.1.45` and .NET SDK 10.0.401.

This is a beta build and it is not code-signed yet, so Windows SmartScreen warns about an
unknown publisher. Check the file before running it (see "Verify a download" in the README):

SHA-256: `2263B393556F8D6DD4412BD0FEA365FE9042F9AA4881D2E7D8EA435904D9B8D0`

Third-party components and their licenses: `THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md` in the repository.
